newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens sign big Japanese polypropylene deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens sign big Japanese polypropylene deal.

text.p: Turkmenistan has signed a $400 million deal with Japan's Itochu Corp, JGC Corp and Nisso Industry Co Ltd to make polypropylene at a Turkmen oil refinery, a state energy official said on Wednesday.

The official, from state oil and gas company Turkmenneftegaz, declined to be identified but told Reuters that polypropylene would be produced at the Turkmenbashi refinery in the western port town of Turkmenbashi on the Caspian Sea.
Polypropylene output would be 90,000 tonnes a year, he said, adding that the product was essential for the automobile and energy sectors. It would be made mostly for export, he said.
He said the project would be financed by a loan from the Japanese government to be paid back in hard-currnecy earnings from polypropylene exports.
The deal was brokered by Israeli company Merhav.
Last year Merhav helped to arrange a $500-million deal to reconstruct the Turkmenbashi refinery by German, Israeli, Iranian, Turkish, French and Japanese companies.
